runner: the entity that travels the maze; a common noun, translate it.
block: a piece the player places to lengthen the path; translate it. User copy always says "block" (never "brick" — that's an internal variable name only).
thunder: the slow-field the player places; translate it. User copy always says "thunder" ("power" and "slow" are internal code terms and never appear on screen). Use your language's word for THUNDER — the storm/sound sense — not lightning: de Donner (not Blitz), zh-Hans 雷电 (not 闪电), es trueno, fr foudre, pt-BR trovão, ja サンダー. Whatever splits.thunderN already uses in that locale is the term; keep every key consistent with it.
daily: the day's ranked puzzle; translate as the noun for the daily challenge.
board: the 20x20 grid a daily is played on — the surface, not the day's puzzle (that's "daily") and not what the player builds on it (that's "maze"/"build"). Translate it; copy uses it only for the grid itself ("Reset board").
maze: the arrangement of blocks and thunders a player builds on a board, and the thing a run is timed on. Translate it. "build" is the same object named as the player's result (see below); prefer the wording the source uses in each message.
build: a player's completed maze, as a result that can be compared and beaten ("your builds", "the day's best maze"). Translate it; it is the noun behind the PB board and the RECORD/BEST badges.
run: one completed attempt: the runner travelling a maze, and the time it scored. Translate it ("Runs", "No runs this day"). A run belongs to a daily attempt or to free play.
free play: unranked replay mode; translate the phrase.
ranked: counts toward the daily result; translate it.
solve: a daily attempt whose maze matches the best any player has built on that daily — the puzzle sense of "solve", not merely finishing. Translate it. It is not permanent (someone can build longer later), but the copy deliberately doesn't say so.
PB: short for personal best — the standings board that ranks players by their best build on a day, beside the DAILY board of ranked results. It is a column header and a two-letter toggle, so keep it as short as your language allows; keep "PB" if that abbreviation is already understood, and stay consistent with badge.pb ("NEW PERSONAL BEST").
SUPREME: a celebratory badge for a sole untied #1 — keep it short and punchy; all-caps if the language allows. The profile also uses it lower-case and plural as a stat label ("Supremes": dailies where this player's build is the top one and nobody has matched it); there, match the sentence case of the labels around it.
RECORD: a badge for a held top build — keep it short; all-caps if the language allows. The profile also uses it lower-case and plural as a stat label ("Records": dailies where the player shares the top build); there, match the sentence case of the labels around it.
BEST: a badge for a personal best — keep it short; all-caps if the language allows.
DELETE: the literal word the user must type to confirm account deletion — keep it as the English word DELETE unless a localized equivalent is unambiguous and standard.
slow: the state a thunder puts the runner in (half speed for 6s). An internal term — copy never names it as a thing; where the effect has to be described, it appears as the plain adjective "slowed" (see splits.wasteTitle).
splits: the per-mark breakdown of a run (speedrunning sense: the time at each point along the route); translate with the term your language's speedrunning/racing communities use.
flag: a marker the player plants on a board to add a split point; translate it as the pennant/marker sense.
